### API Rate Limits
The current rate limit on paid usage plans is **30 requests per second** [the-odds-api.com](https://the-odds-api.com/guide/rate-limit.html) [the-odds-api.com](https://the-odds-api.com/liveapi/guides/v4/api-error-codes.html). 

If the rate limit is exceeded, the API returns an `EXCEEDED_FREQ_LIMIT` error (HTTP status code 429) [the-odds-api.com](https://the-odds-api.com/liveapi/guides/v4/api-error-codes.html). However, 429 errors can still occur even if you are sending requests below the 30 requests/second limit for the following reasons:
1.  **Traffic Spikes:** If the system receives a sudden large increase in traffic, it may take a few minutes to scale up, temporarily knocking back requests with 429s [the-odds-api.com](https://the-odds-api.com/guide/rate-limit.html).
2.  **Network Conditions:** Servers receive requests at a different rate than they are sent due to network variations. For example, sending exactly 30 requests per second over 2 seconds might result in the server receiving 25 in the first second and 33 in the next second (meaning 3 requests get rate-limited) [the-odds-api.com](https://the-odds-api.com/guide/rate-limit.html).

**Best Practices for Rate Limits:**
*   Expect 429s occasionally, especially when operating close to the limit, and retry the request after a couple of seconds [the-odds-api.com](https://the-odds-api.com/guide/rate-limit.html).
*   Space requests out over a longer time period rather than sending short bursts [the-odds-api.com](https://the-odds-api.com/guide/rate-limit.html).
*   Combine multiple markets or regions into a single request rather than making one request per market/region [the-odds-api.com](https://the-odds-api.com/guide/rate-limit.html).
*   Cache responses and make less frequent requests to endpoints that don't update often, such as `/sports` and `/events` [the-odds-api.com](https://the-odds-api.com/guide/rate-limit.html).
*   Be mindful of usage quota costs, as different endpoints carry different credit costs [the-odds-api.com](https://the-odds-api.com/manage/troubleshoot-unexpected-usage.html). You can monitor your usage via the HTTP response headers: `x-requests-remaining`, `x-requests-used`, and `x-requests-last` [the-odds-api.com](https://the-odds-api.com/liveapi/guides/v4/api-error-codes.html).

**Source: [github.com/Ecart-type/devig](https://github.com/Ecart-type/devig/blob/main/README.md)**
This repository implements four standard devigging algorithms, noting that they "disagree with each other" and must be tested empirically:
*   **Multiplicative:** Equivalent to the proportional method; assumes margin is taken in proportion to price. Recommended for two-way markets.
*   **Additive:** Subtracts an equal amount from each implied probability. Risky for longshots as it can result in negative probabilities.
*   **Power:** Solves $\sum q_i^k = 1$; assumes longshots carry more margin. Recommended for three-way markets (e.g., Soccer 1X2).
*   **Shin:** Models the margin as protection against insider trading.

*   **No Explicit Free Tier Rate Limit:** Unlike paid tiers, the free tier does not have a published "requests per minute" limit. Developers must rely on the `x-requests-remaining` header to manage usage and avoid hitting the monthly cap or triggering burst protection.
*   **Historical Data Costs:** Because historical odds cost 10× more credits than live odds, the 500-credit free allowance is exhausted very quickly if used for historical data (e.g., one request for 1 market and 1 region costs 10 credits, allowing only 50 such calls per month).
*   **Account Management:** Usage credits and subscription changes are managed through the accounts portal. Even if a user has an active subscription, they may need to create a new account structure to access certain management features.
